items.title: Assessment Q1 — Role of electrical energy
question_paragraphs: Explain the role of electrical energy in modern life and various engineering branches.
paragraphs: Electrical energy plays a central role in modern life because it can be generated from many sources, transmitted over long distances, distributed conveniently, and converted easily into light, heat, sound and mechanical power.

In everyday life it is used for lighting, fans, refrigeration, air conditioning, water pumping, cooking appliances, communication systems, computers, mobile charging, medical equipment and public services. Because control is easy and operation is clean at the point of use, electrical energy has become the most convenient form of energy for homes, institutions and industries.

In industry, electrical energy drives motors, machine tools, pumps, compressors, conveyor systems, welding sets, furnaces, electroplating units and automated production lines. Its precise control makes it suitable for measurement, protection, instrumentation and modern process control.

Electrical energy is important in many engineering branches. In electrical engineering it is the basic subject for generation, transmission, distribution and utilization. In mechanical engineering it powers drives, electric heating and control systems. In civil engineering it is needed for lighting, lifts, pumps, HVAC systems and building services. In electronics and communication engineering it powers circuits, embedded systems and communication equipment. In computer and IT fields it supports computers, servers, data centres and networking. In chemical, biomedical, agricultural and other branches it is essential for process plants, laboratory instruments, hospital equipment, irrigation pumps and automation.
Thus, electrical energy is indispensable in both modern life and engineering practice because of its flexibility, cleanliness, ease of control and wide range of applications.
items.final_answer: Electrical energy is an indispensable, easily controllable and widely usable form of energy for domestic life, industry and almost every branch of engineering.

items.title: Assessment Q2 — Current through 2 Ω using Thevenin’s theorem
question_paragraphs: Find the current flowing through the 2-ohm resistor connected between the points \(a\) and \(b\) using Thevenin’s theorem.

textbook_match.label: Exact textbook match
textbook_match.note: This class question matches prescribed-textbook Example 1.9.3. The class-note dropdown keeps the canonical link and also shows the requested NRS worked-solution sheet.

figures.alt: Notebook-style NRS worked solution for Assessment Question 2 showing the given bridge circuit, the open-circuit calculation of Vth, the short-circuited network used to find Rth, the Thevenin equivalent circuit and the final current through the 2-ohm resistor.
figures.caption: Class-note redraw · Thevenin solution sheet for Assessment Q2

paragraphs: Treat the 2-ohm resistor between \(a\) and \(b\) as the load and remove it to find the Thevenin equivalent seen from terminals \(a\) and \(b\).
With the load removed, the upper branch current is \(I_1=\dfrac{12}{4+6}=1.2\,\text{A}\). Hence the node voltage at \(a\) is \(V_a=I_1\times 6=7.2\,\text{V}\).
The lower branch current is \(I_2=\dfrac{12}{3+5}=1.5\,\text{A}\). Hence the node voltage at \(b\) is \(V_b=I_2\times 5=7.5\,\text{V}\).
Therefore the Thevenin voltage is \(V_{th}=V_{ab}=V_a-V_b=7.2-7.5=-0.3\,\text{V}\). This means point \(b\) is at a higher potential than point \(a\).
To find \(R_{th}\), replace the 12 V source by a short circuit. Then \(R_{th}=(4\parallel 6)+(3\parallel 5)=\dfrac{4\times 6}{4+6}+\dfrac{3\times 5}{3+5}=2.4+1.875=4.275\,\Omega\).
Reconnect the 2-ohm load. The total series resistance is \(R_{th}+R_L=4.275+2=6.275\,\Omega\).

Hence the load-current magnitude is \(I=\dfrac{|V_{th}|}{R_{th}+R_L}=\dfrac{0.3}{6.275}=0.0478\,\text{A}=47.8\,\text{mA}\). Since \(b\) is at the higher potential, the actual current through the 2-ohm resistor flows from \(b\) to \(a\).
items.final_answer: \(I=47.8\,\text{mA}\) flowing from \(b\) to \(a\). If referenced from \(a\) to \(b\), \(I_{ab}=-47.8\,\text{mA}\).
